description: Checks whether USGS has recorded an earthquake that someone who just felt shaking a few minutes ago could have felt: large and close enough for an estimated intensity of MMI 2+ at their location (Atkinson & Wald 2007, the equation USGS Did You Feel It? uses). Answers yes (with the event), not_yet_reported (nothing yet, but small quakes take minutes to be catalogued, so this is not a no), or no; smaller quakes recorded nearby are listed as too small to feel. The result links USGS Did You Feel It? for reporting shaking. Data: USGS, as held by QuakeIndex. Each result includes its source, when the data was last confirmed, and links to the QuakeIndex and USGS event pages. No predictions and no warnings: results name ShakeAlert and MyShake as the sources of earthquake early warning.

city.description: US town or city, e.g. 'Ridgecrest'. Add state.

latitude.description: Decimal degrees. Give with longitude, OR use zip, OR city.

minutes_ago.description: Roughly how long ago the shaking was felt.

state.description: Two-letter code or name, with city.

name: was_that_an_earthquake
title: Was that an earthquake?
